key_insight: AI for semen analysis is moving from single-task image recognition toward multimodal, clinically translatable decision support across sperm detection, motility, morphology, and genetic integrity.
clinical_relevance: If validated robustly, these tools could make semen assessment more objective, reproducible, and scalable for infertility diagnosis and assisted reproductive technology planning.
method: Computer vision for sperm detection, counting, segmentation, and morphology/defect classification
Tracking-based analysis for motility and functional assessment in time-lapse microscopy
Multimodal fusion of images, videos, CASA metrics, DNA integrity assays, and clinical metadata
evidence_signal: The review synthesizes public datasets, benchmarks, and evaluation metrics, while emphasizing performance testing across multicenter and clinically oriented validation stages.
watch_item: Real-world use is constrained by data scarcity, cross-center domain shift, annotation inconsistency, and the need for careful calibration and workflow integration.
paper_title: Deep Learning for Semen Analysis in Male Infertility: Computer Vision, Multimodal Fusion, and Clinical Translation
